newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian T-bill yield premiums seen with new tax.
newsitem.headline: Russian T-bill yield premiums seen with new tax.

text.p: The premium on yields at Wednesday's discount GKO Treasury bill auctions will be five to seven percent on the highest accepted price, following a new 15 percent earnings tax on government securities, dealers said.
The Justice Ministry on Tuesday approved a request by the Finance Ministry to treat earnings from T-bills as interest, which qualifies for a 15 percent tax rate.
Dealers forecast the yield on six-month T-bill series 22069 in the 34.95-36.99 percent range and 35.22-38.82 percent on six-month T-bill series 22070.

Alexei Orekhov from Renaissance Capital said foreigners were unlikely to have managed to transfer money for Wednesday's auctions and that Russian banks would try to take advantage of this by hiking up yields.
"Russian banks will try to get an extra margin and its justified level is three to four percent," he said.
"But as taxed paper is being placed for the first time, it is quite possible that the yield will be five to seven percent above the market level at the highest accepted price."
Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said the new tax would cause only a slight stir on the market, which he said would soon wind down as the government seeks cheaper ways to raise debt.
Robert Devane, government borrowing expert at Troika Dialog, said Western investors were interested in buying the new paper to arbitrage profits against the new tax.
He forecast solid demand at Wednesday's sale.

"But the best days will be Thursday and Friday, when the regulation is published and secondary trading takes place," he said. "The purchase of the paper at the auction is a trip to a dark room with closed eyes, and the main investment decisions will be taken only after secondary trading."
